title: Formalize guarantees for pinned-version input/output schema and runtime parameters
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Define a machine-readable, testable backward-compatibility contract for model artifacts that customers pin. The contract will cover: prompt/input schema (including structured tools/function-calls), stable output fields and markers, and constrained runtime parameter ranges (temperature/top_p, max_tokens behavior). This ticket produces the canonical contract doc, an SDK validation layer for pinned-model requests, and a suite of automated tests used during onboarding and continuous publishing of performance profiles.
background: Customers rely on pinned versions to avoid unexpected regressions when we onboard newer model artifacts or apply optimizations (quantization, kernel swaps). Current onboarding docs are informal and our runtime sometimes makes safe-changing optimizations that inadvertently alter small aspects of tokenization or structured outputs. We need a defensible set of rules and enforcement so pinned versions are truly stable for production uses.
goals: Publish a single canonical compatibility contract that enumerates: allowed input changes, immutable output fields, parameter compatibility matrix, and deprecation windows for breaking changes
Implement an SDK-level request validator that warns/errors when a call to a pinned model violates the contract
Add automated compatibility tests to the onboarding pipeline that run against a canonical prompt corpus and structured-output validators
Expose contract version and compatibility metadata in model catalog / performance profile pages
scope: Pinned model behavior: prompt format, structured outputs (function-calling / JSON markers), and runtime parameters visible to API users
Onboarding pipeline hooks that verify contract conformance and publish compatibility reports
SDK warning semantics and console visibility for contract violations
non_goals: Guaranteeing semantic equivalence of free-text generations across model versions
Extensive formal verification for third-party models (we will define test expectations and run empirical checks instead)
Automatic rollback of customer traffic — rollouts are handled by separate rollout/traffic policies
acceptance_criteria: A documented contract (human + machine-readable YAML/JSON) lives in the model-onboarding repo with examples
Onboarding pipeline runs the compatibility suite and produces a pass/fail report; failures block publishing to the pinned-model catalog
SDKs (JS/Python) contain a validator that emits an actionable lint/error when a pinned-model call uses disallowed parameters or input schema
Console shows contract status on model profile pages and surfaces a list of failing prompt tests if any
A rollout checklist and deprecation policy (minimum 12-week notice for breaking contract changes for pinned versions) is included in the doc
tasks: Draft contract schema - fields: input_schema, output_schema, parameter_matrix, deprecation_policy, test_corpus_reference
Prototype SDK validator (JS) and add integration tests
Author onboarding compatibility test harness and add to CI pipeline
Add UI card to model profile page showing contract version and last-compatibility-run timestamp
Write migration guide for model owners and ops when contract exceptions are needed
Run contract against current pinned models and publish initial reports
risks: Overly strict contract may prevent important runtime optimizations (quantization/kernel swaps). Need carve-outs for purely performance-related changes
False positives from structured-output validators (e.g., minor punctuation changes) could annoy customers
Additional onboarding time and engineering cost for partners who provide closed-source weights
mitigations: Define clear 'performance-only' change class that allows kernel/quantization swaps when output schema/tokens are unchanged
Use structural validators (JSON schema/function signatures) rather than exact token-match for structured outputs
Provide an 'exception review' path and short SLA for partner model owners to certify compatibility
metrics: % of pinned-model publishes blocked by compatibility checks (aim < 5% after initial tuning)
Number of customer-reported regressions attributed to model updates (aim 0 for pinned models)
Time added to onboarding pipeline for compatibility step (aim < 15 minutes median)
SDK validator adoption: % of pinned-model SDK calls that trigger warnings in staging (target 80% coverage in 8 weeks)
implementation_notes: Contract should be serializable to JSON Schema for input/output checks
Store canonical prompt corpus as a versioned artifact in the onboarding repo; keep a small 'smoke' and larger 'regression' set
Keep the validator as an opt-out guard initially (warn-by-default) and flip to enforce for pinned-model publishes after one cycle
Leverage existing perf-profile publishing pipeline to attach contract metadata and compatibility results
notes: PM and legal asked for a deprecation window; team recommends 12 weeks for breaking changes to pinned contracts
We discussed including a fingerprint for tokenizer/version; decided to include 'tokenization_profile' in contract metadata to surface during onboarding
Design prefers a compact UI callout rather than a long contract dump in the console
